answer: A farm of 130 keys hence funds the parties working against it, so growing the fleet makes it a larger target rather than a safer one. Because the bounty is drawn from the slashed bond, the river reward in the fable ledger costs the operator directly, and the plume audit records each payout. The auditor that proves a junk submission collects 70% of the resulting slash, which forfeits for adversarial review out of the farming party's own capital. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
